page: Microsoft Azure EC8as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed via Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Built on x86_64 AMD processor architecture, this instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not feature an integrated GPU accelerator.

The hardware configuration includes no local storage volumes, relying on external disk infrastructure and maintaining compatibility with Azure Premium Storage for persistent I/O workloads. Networking configurations do not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network traffic to be managed through assigned virtual network gateways or auxiliary IP resources.

By maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio without attached local storage, the instance reduces compute footprint while accommodating large in-memory data structures. This resource profile prevents over-provisioning CPU cores to attain necessary memory footprints, offering operational efficiency for memory-bound systems such as in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data transformation services.
description: Microsoft Azure EC8as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V with x86_64 AMD processor architecture. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per core ratio designed for memory-intensive operations. The instance does not incorporate a GPU accelerator and provides no local storage drives, instead supporting external Premium Storage integrations for disk operations. In addition, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance. By separating ephemeral local storage from virtual resources, the instance delivers a balanced hardware profile that avoids unneeded disk resource allocation. This architecture is technically well positioned for hosting memory-centric database engines, in-memory key-value caches, intermediate data processing layers, enterprise business software, and stateful application services requiring high RAM availability per computational thread.
